# Owners and access lists read on GitHub's Windows machines, through one handle on each name (CreateFileW with
# backup semantics and open-reparse-point, GetSecurityInfo owner+list, then the system's own text for it). Every
# line is WHOLE, as read. A user's own SID is replaced by a made-up one
# (S-1-5-21-1004336348-1177238915-682003330-1001) and a user's folder name by `someone`; nothing else is changed.
# The long S-1-5-80-956008885-... is TrustedInstaller (the system's own installer). S-1-15-2-2 and the S-1-15-3-...
# values are app-package and capability names; AC is all app packages. Format: PATH <newline> KIND; OWNER-AND-LIST

# What a plain user (made for the run, not an administrator, removed after it) could do, the same on both machines:
#   GitHub's Python (C:\hostedtoolcache\...): write beside the interpreter DONE; into site-packages DONE; into the
#     raqib folder DONE
#   C:\Program Files: write REFUSED; give it another name REFUSED
#   C:\Program Files\RaqibProbe8 (a packed Raqib an administrator copied there): write beside the program REFUSED;
#     into _internal REFUSED; to raqib.exe REFUSED; give the folder another name REFUSED; run raqib.exe DONE
#   C:\ : make a folder at the root DONE (it is then his, with the list above)
#
# The rights words in these texts, as the file system means them (the letters are the directory service's):
#   CC 0x1 read/list   DC 0x2 write/add file   LC 0x4 append/add folder   SW 0x8 read ext. attrs
#   RP 0x10 write ext. attrs   WP 0x20 execute/traverse   DT 0x40 delete child   LO 0x80 read attrs
#   CR 0x100 write attrs   SD 0x10000 delete   RC 0x20000 read control   WD 0x40000 write list   WO 0x80000 write owner
#   GA 0x10000000  GX 0x20000000  GW 0x40000000  GR 0x80000000
#   FA 0x1f01ff  FR 0x120089  FW 0x120116  FX 0x1200a0     (0x1301bf is `modify`; 0x1200a9 is read and execute)
